champion: Cystoid Macular Edema secondary to Intraocular Lens
ordered_diagnoses: Cystoid Macular Edema secondary to Intraocular Lens

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral visual disturbance with signs of intraocular inflammation and macular edema
salient_findings: Blurry vision in one eye for several months
Cystoid macular edema with subfoveal fluid in the affected eye
Keratic precipitates and cells in the anterior chamber
key_facts: Blurry vision in right eye for several months
On anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years
Conjunctival injection and fine keratic precipitates in right eye
Cystoid macular edema with yellow spot in fovea in right eye
No peripheral inflammation in either eye
Normal blood tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders
Unremarkable computed tomography of the chest

s4.champion: Cystoid Macular Edema secondary to Intraocular Lens

raw.champion: Cystoid Macular Edema secondary to Intraocular Lens
raw.rationale: The patient has a history of bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens and presents with cystoid macular edema, which is a known complication of intraocular lens implantation.

rejected.label: Anastrozole-induced Macular Edema
rejected.why: While the patient is on anastrozole therapy, there is no strong evidence to suggest a direct link between anastrozole and macular edema in this case.

rejected.label: Intermediate Uveitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not show significant signs of intermediate uveitis, such as vitritis or peripheral inflammation.

rejected.label: Uveitic Macular Edema
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of bilateral iritis, the current presentation is more consistent with cystoid macular edema secondary to intraocular lens rather than uveitic macular edema.

rejected.label: Fuchs Heterochromic Iridocyclitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not match the typical characteristics of Fuchs Heterochromic Iridocyclitis, such as heterochromia of the iris or a history of chronic iridocyclitis.
